reading.body:
Meta's Rutherford County campus in North Carolina has no published power capacity or building count. The operator reports a $750M+ investment since groundbreaking in 2010, which suggests a mature multi-building hyperscale site, but without disclosed megawatts, rack counts, or accelerator density, the campus's contribution to AI scaling cannot be quantified from published data.

Meta states the campus will employ 275+ in operational jobs and is matched with 100 percent clean and renewable energy as part of global net-zero operations. The campus operational buildings achieve LEED Gold certification. A separate Meta-supported project is adding 310 megawatts of new renewable energy in North Carolina, but the amount allocated to this campus is not disclosed.

Among the 19 mapped facilities in North Carolina, only five have published power capacity on operator spec pages. This campus ranks 6th by published megawatts in the state, but that ranking reflects only the five disclosed figures, not the actual size hierarchy. Without published capacity, the Rutherford County site cannot be assessed as a binding constraint on grid or AI scaling relative to other North Carolina facilities or the national fleet.
